questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The understandable language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, the amounts of other erasmus students helped a bit as I wasn't good at finding it myself

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Overall, we were helped all through the process

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were some minor difficulties in regards to the housing but it worked out

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's no problem at all, the city isn't that big

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Classic student housing

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very welcoming. All of the erasmus studetns met up at the uni center and we were talked – throughly – through the whole process

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student center offered help all through out the week

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: That was very accescible

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions and don't postpone doing all the practical stuff. Just get it done right away.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Slighty lower ambitional level then what I've experienced at UCPH – however the courses was still very interresting

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took BA courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think the general experience from my peers form UCPH was that the level of ambition was slightly lower but not to a degree that was bad. To be honest I think it was very pleasent when I also had to manage moving to a new country and meeting new people.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Music, Gender and Sexuality 
Art, Architecture and Visual Culture 1950-today

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Music, Gender and Sexuality was my favourite. I would recommend any course with Stephen Amico. His teaching style was very inspiring to me.

questions.answer: Nothing unexpected, but Fitness and Transportation was necessary for me

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is slightly more expensive than in Denmark – especially vegetables and beers

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great options – especially if you like bouldering

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Music festivals, gym, choirs, bouldering, hikes, fishing – there was so many options at the student fair

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes with your new friends; it's an easy way to get to know each other. And when you've gotten to know each other, then go on hike to the DNT cabins up further in the mountains: it's a must!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There was an outdoor cinema which was very cute and be aware of all the art happening around the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Feels very similar

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs or any other forms of social gatherings that are not only for Erasmus students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor culture is amazing: you'll quickly be drawn to it

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Yes, there is a lot of rain, but it is not as extreme as everyone tells you – just get a good raincoat
2. Choose some courses that actually interest you and/or are a little easier – this will make the socialising a lot more manageable
3. Use nature as much as you can. When the weather is clear – get out!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stop overromantisizing getting local freinds and/or living in a particular local spot. Just be present and talk with the people around you. If you meet some local people, that's nice, but just let it all happen.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting three really good freinds (all of them danish) and enjoying the nature

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my family

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
